correctness.rationale: The ASM row/column prefix characterization is equivalent to the full definition. Exhaustion of exactly eight possible rows to fourfold products gives all 42 configurations; their distinct nine-bit reductions are injective. Each full support has odd row/column parities, hence lies in a dimension-nine affine coset, with 128-fold dual-frequency magnitudes. Direct character sums and exact Walsh butterflies agree for all 512 reduced frequencies, and all 65,536 ambient coefficients were separately summed. Reduced absolute histogram totals 512, zero count 120, Parseval sum 21,504. The full rank is 128(512-120)=50,176. An exact second butterfly of the nonzero-support indicator has absolute sum 3,184, giving the normalized projection-kernel l1 norm 3,184/512=199/32. Translation conjugation and averaging is a valid no-norm-increase argument on l1 and linfinity; the unique commuting projection has multiplier one precisely on the convolution range.

originality.rationale: The accepted claim is the evaluated all-frequency Walsh distribution and sharp endpoint projection norm of the full 42-state order-four ASM binary nonzero-support set. Classical unsigned count, symmetry enumeration, partial row refinements, weighted ASM six-vertex partition functions and generic translation averaging are excluded from originality. The most relevant primary sections were inspected and actual published-finding corpus and broader literature queries did not identify a dominating evaluated result. A generic site-weighted identity may indirectly encode the 512 numbers, but this would not automatically give their exact evaluated histogram and sharp norm; residual priority risk is recorded.

value.rationale: Order four is the first nontrivial even ASM size after two permutation matrices at order two; an exact natural 42-point Fourier invariant is motivated by combinatorial convolution and recovery. The complete 13-level absolute spectrum, nullity 15,360 and sharp Banach projection constant 199/32 are not entailed by the unsigned count 42. The sharp endpoint norm quantifies the cost of stable range projection for the concrete first nontrivial ASM family, a substantive exact finite spectral classification. The claim does not require a speculative all-order theorem and expressly avoids presenting a known-cardinality recomputation as its novelty.
